newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada spot natgas prices seen climbing higher.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot natgas prices seen climbing higher.

text.p: Alberta spot natural gas prices stand to climb higher amid icy weather in the province and strong demand in California, despite an already sharp runup in prices, traders said on Thursday.

To the delight of Canadian producers, day-to-day gas at Alberta's AECO storage hub rose to about C$2 per gigajoule on Thursday, up about five cents from Wednesday. December gas jumped to as high as C$2.07 per GJ from C$1.88 the day before.
Alberta gas prices had not climbed above C$2 since the coldest days of last winter, and trading sources say another 20 cents could be gained by early next week.
"That's why we're rubbing our hands with glee -- because colder weather will still come," said a gas marketing manager with a large Calgary-based producer.

Marketers said current strong prices were the result of several factors, including high domestic demand as temperatures drop, shorter-than-expected supply and a big draw from California utilities as AECO gas competes with that from the San Juan Basin in the South western United States, where prices have also been strong.

Despite the withdrawal of about 700 million cubic feet of gas per day from all three Alberta facilities for the last three days, volumes for sale in the province have been below expectations, said a Calgary marketer.
He said NOVA Gas Transmission Ltd's system system has struggled to meet its line pack with receipts being about 200 MMCFD below target.
Adding to the tight supplies has been electrical difficulties experienced at several gas plants in Alberta as frost wreaked havoc with power lines, the marketer said.
Sources agreed that prices could by as much as 20 cents by Monday, when southern Alberta temperatures fall to a forecast low of -26 Celsius (-15 Fahrenheit).

The producer said several more expensive natural gas production projects could be activated in Alberta and northeast British Columbia if current price levels are sustained. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
